assumptions: The input y ranges over all real numbers. No random variable or gate is part of this definition.
units.title: The paper's energy truncation
units.statement: Integrate the even unit cutoff from zero to the input, then rescale by positive n, β and λ. This is the literal function U from the source, not a freely chosen odd function.
units.reader_note: This definition is a prerequisite, not a new proved inequality. All parameters have positive types; there is no fallback at zero.

steps.title: Use the exact smooth cutoff
steps.text: The source function ρ is Mathlib's expNegInvGlue. Substituting z=2−|s| in smoothTransition gives 1−z=|s|−1, so the quotient is the existing smoothUnitCutoff. Its denominator is strictly positive everywhere; its value lies in [0,1] and it is even.
steps.lean: The definition writes the rho quotient literally. A private proof identifies it with Cutoff.smoothUnitCutoff using smoothUnitCutoff_eq_smoothTransition and Real.smoothTransition.pos_denom.

steps.title: Integrate and rescale
steps.text: The integral is oriented: for negative t, integration from zero to t reverses sign. Continuity of the kernel ensures ordinary interval integrability. Positive parameters make both scaling factors well-defined.
steps.lean: ℕ+ encodes a positive integer. Each subtype {r : ℝ // 0 < r} carries a real value together with its positivity proof. intervalIntegral uses signed endpoints, not an unordered interval.

units.lean_statement: The public carrier admits only positive n, β and lam and arbitrary real y. The Lean binder lam denotes the source's λ.
units.lean_proof: Definitions compute mathematical objects; they do not themselves prove estimates. The adjacent theorem proves the properties actually needed for Fact10 from this body.
units.dependency_notes: The body is a literal source formula. The following theorem reuses Samplinglib's canonical cutoff; source text is attributed separately from code provenance.

units.boundary: This is the literal scalar energy load and Fact10. The recursive selection of amplitudes, higher smoothness/cap/plateau properties, coefficient fields and conditional product iteration are separate. Lemma6.2 and all main lower bounds remain open.
assumptions: Y has a centered Gaussian probability law, including variance zero.
The deterministic gate a lies in [0,1].
units.title: Gaussian bound for the actual truncated load
units.statement: For positive integer n and positive β,λ, define ρ(t)=exp(−1/t) for t>0 and zero otherwise, φ(t)=∫₀ᵗ ρ(2−|s|)/(ρ(2−|s|)+ρ(|s|−1)) ds, and U(y)=nβ²/λ·φ(λy/(nβ)). If Y is centered Gaussian, possibly degenerate, and a∈[0,1], then exp(−aU(Y)) is integrable and E exp(−aU(Y))≤exp(β² Var(Y)/2). This scalar statement permits any positive β,λ; the paper's recursive choices are a later instantiation.
units.reader_note: No oddness, continuity, sublinearity or integrability hypothesis is supplied: the proof derives all of them from the literal source function.

steps.title: Derive the primitive's properties
steps.text: The even kernel k is continuous and between zero and one. Replacing s by −s in the oriented integral gives φ(−t)=−φ(t). The integral norm bound gives |φ(t)|≤|t| for both signs of t. The fundamental theorem of calculus gives continuity, hence measurability.
steps.lean: Private helpers use the existing cutoff's continuity and range; integral_comp_neg handles the sign reversal, norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const gives the bound, and differentiable_integral_of_continuous gives continuity.

steps.title: Scale without losing the constant
steps.text: Both scale factors are positive. Oddness is preserved under scaling, and the factors n and λ cancel exactly in the absolute-value estimate. Composition and multiplication preserve continuity.
steps.lean: Positivity is extracted from the parameter types. Field cancellation is justified by nonzero n, β and lam; these are not silently assumed by automation.

steps.title: Apply the Gaussian comparison and transport the law
steps.text: The established load properties satisfy the reviewed odd-load comparison: symmetry turns the exponential into cosh, sublinearity compares with the linear load, and the Gaussian MGF gives exp(β²v/2). The HasLaw hypothesis transports both the integral and integrability to Y's probability space. The same law identity yields Var(Y)=v, including v=0.
steps.formula: \begin{gathered}\int e^{-aU(y)}\,\mathcal N(0,v)(dy)\le e^{\beta^2v/2},\\\mathbb E_P e^{-aU(Y)}=\int e^{-aU(y)}\,\mathcal N(0,v)(dy),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_P(Y)=v.\end{gathered}
steps.lean: gaussian_odd_load_bound is the existing Samplinglib parent. HasLaw.integral_comp and Integrable.comp_aemeasurable transport actual integrability, while HasLaw.variance_eq and variance_id_gaussianReal identify the variance. No conditional expectation is involved.

units.lean_statement: HasLaw includes a.e. measurability of Y and equality of its pushforward measure to gaussianReal 0 v. It also forces P to be a probability measure, so no redundant instance or moment assumption appears.
units.lean_proof: The private calculations construct the hypotheses of the existing Gaussian comparison inside the proof. The public result contains actual Bochner integrability as well as the bound; totalized integrals do not replace analytical obligations.
units.dependency_notes: The cutoff and Gaussian comparison are ASTIS-owned existing parents; interval calculus and law transport are pinned Mathlib. Conditional factorization is a planned consumer, not a solid current Lean edge.
